   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  July 10, 2025

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Secretary Esquivel

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Executive Assistant
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, Secretary Cynthia Esquivel and Commissioner Edgar Pelayo.
Staff: Director of Parks & Recreation Steve Costley, Deputy Director Tina Fierro, and Parks Superintendent
Glenn Massey.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident, received an email from California Endowment informing him
of there will be applications for competitive grants being accepted, has asked Council to apply to get
money for a splash pad at SG Park. How could they build the Urban Orchard Park which cost $29 million yet
can’t afford a $2 million splash pad when surrounding cities are building them.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. HAS ANNUAL REPORT FOR 2024
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley introduced Catherine Villanueva, Director of Pasitos Programs, she reviewed this item; a
discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked how many years have they been in SG and how do they get their
information out. They’ve been here 15 years, and mostly word of mouth and social media. Commissioner
Pelayo asked what other communities they service? The southeast and other cities. Chair Flores thanked
her for the report.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident, liked the report, would it be possible for them to provide a
computer lab for our residents? Also, they should be paying a rental fee for their use of the resource
centers.

2. ORAL REPORT REGARDING QUIMBY FEES
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Pelayo
Director Costley introduced Community Development Director Gabriel Perez; he reviewed the report. He
handed the Commissioners and staff a printout with details on Quimby Fees which are fees that a
developer pays to improve city parks or donate land to create a park; a discussion ensued.

CHAIR FLORES LEFT DURING THIS PORTION OF THE MEETING

Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident, thank Director Perez, wants to know when was the last time
the City collected Quimby fees? And can they be used for park enhancement and splash pads and can fees
be collected on franchise businesses? Director Costley stated that the City does not have or every had
Quimby fees; Council would have to create an ordinance. And Quimby fees cannot be charged to
franchises/businesses.

3. ORAL REPORT ON UPDATE OF THE PARKS & RECREATION MASTER PLAN
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
  Page 1 of 3
  4
 M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Secretary Esquivel
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Even though there isn’t an update Master Plan
there have been various improvements

Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident, since no there’s no new Master Plan what’s being done to
distribute the survey? Director Costley explained what is being done.

Recognized: Jimmy Ozaeta, SG resident, interested in how many surveys have been completed. And how
is it being distributed to residents. Deputy Dir. De La Rosa stated all the measures staff is taking to
promote the survey.

4. ANNUAL REPORT ON CULTURAL AND ART PROGRAMS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo to approve the proposed meeting schedule with the changes
suggested by Chair Flores.
Deputy Dir. De La Rosa reviewed this item; going over all the special and yearly events, and the success of
new events staff organized. In Youth Programming, Tot Time and Tiny Two’s classes fluctuated quarterly
due to staff shortages. There was a new event Trunk or Treat for the pre-schools classes which was a hit
with everyone. Teen Programs have been on hold, a Full Time Recreation Coordinator was hired in June
and the program will start to be revamped. At the Senior Center the HSA lunch program continues to be
successful. Yoga, Loteria, and a mental health support group was started. Also an ESL class geared for
seniors began and HSA started offering easy recipe options for them to try at home. The Contract Classes
offering Baby Boogie, Folklorico, ballet, Hip Hop classes to name a few continues to reach maximum
capacity. The Golf Course has welcomed several new members along with the local high school teams
having their practices and matches. We hosted four golf tournaments that drew in large crowds. Cultural
Arts hosted their 3rd Annual Zine Fiesta and the opening of Press Repeat/Oir de Nuevo exhibit. New this
quarter was open studio Saturdays and themed drop-in art activities. Staff participated in the Chicxs
Rockerxs SELA’s tenth anniversary. Arts for LA Activate program came to an end and our team organized
the final event, Art & Picnic - Picnic at the Museum! held at our Museum & Art Gallery. We hosted an art
exhibit, the LA Times wrote an article about CRSELA’s work and exhibition. Our staff created a playlist in
celebration of the exhibit and NBC 4 highlighted the exhibit in one of their segments. In the Spring new
classes were added; Toddler Art Club and Art Club for Adults. They were so popular they will be a regular
classes. A discussion ensued.
Commissioner Pelayo asked if volunteers can be used to operate services that will be affected by budget
cuts; Director Costley explained there are legalities to having adult volunteers around children.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez SG resident, stated he would like staff to put on burlesque and magic
shows in the Auditorium.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Council hasn’t approved the budget, for now the Golf Course will be closed Monday and
Tuesday, the Pool on Fridays, and there’s a hold on Fee Waivers until the July 22 Council meeting.

Deputy Dir. De La Rosa: The Summer Kick Off event was June 11 and was very successful with 400
participants. Balling After Dark was July 2; Fun Run will be next week, with 500 people registered.
Upcoming events are Family Camp Out Night in August and Family Magic Show in September.

Parks Supt. Massey: At this time of the year Grounds Maintenance staff concentrates on irrigation and
fixing broken valves to maintain the parks.

 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Vice Chair Ruiz: Why will the pool be closed on Fridays, Deputy Dir. De La Rosa replied that day will have
the least impact on the patrons.

Commissioner Pelayo: Asked about the special needs issue with the restroom at Cesar Chavez Park.
Director Costley explained that the child has sensory issues, and dirty restrooms are one of his triggers.
Staff does what they can to make sure the restrooms are clean, but that is not always possible due to the
amount of use and the homeless issues. He has also spoke with the mother and explained this to her.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS - Commissioner Pelayo asked for the MOU with Legacy High
School and the Fee Waiver policy.

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:44 p.m. Vice Chair Ruiz asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Secretary Esquivel

Respectfully submitted:

Cynthia Esquivel, Secretary

  September 11, 2025
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  James Markel, Recreation Manager
Date:  August 21, 2025

Subject:  Annual Sports and Aquatics Division Report

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary:

Aquatics Report
The Aquatics Division is proud to report another successful and impactful year spanning
from Summer 2024 through Spring 2025. This period was marked by increased
community participation, program innovation, improved safety protocols, and strong
staff development.

The year began with an extremely busy Summer 2024 season, highlighted by an almost
20% increase in swim program enrollment compared to the previous summer. More
than 2,800 individuals participated, reflecting a growing demand for water safety, swim
instruction, and specialized aquatic programs. Our most popular program, Learn-to-
Swim (consisting of Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim lessons for all ages) was at
full capacity every month. Our Summer Splash Camp for Kids saw a 20% increase in
participation and had close to 100 participants. We also gained traction with our aquatic
sports programs like Junior Water Polo, Junior Lifeguard, Surfing 101, and Gators Swim
Academy. We continued to host competitive swim teams South Gate Aqua Coalition
(SGAC), Penguins Aquatic Club (PAC), and Lynwood Marlins (LMST), providing over
250 hours of practice time for approximately 200 kids. With expanded hours, we were
able to bring back seasonal aquatic fitness programs in addition to offering our year-
round fitness and therapy classes; our line-up featured SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics,
Masters Swim, Open Play Water Polo and Aqua Blast. To promote these programs, we
presented our first ever Aquatic Fitness Expo and launched the Splash Fitness
membership. Summer is an extremely popular season for party rentals as well, and we
were able to accommodate over 20 private parties. We also offered free water safety
awareness events throughout the summer, including the World’s Largest Swimming
Lesson in June and three Community Swim Days: Summer Kick-Off Splash event in
June, 4th of July Splash event in July, and Back-to-School Splash event in August.
These special events cumulatively brought in around 500 community members. Overall

  Page 1 of 6
  7
 attendance remained high, with over 30,000 visits recorded during the summer months
for Lap Swim, Adult Swim and Family Swim sessions.

During the fall months, our indoor aquatic programming continued to thrive. While we
offer fewer programs in the off-season, our Learn-to-Swim program maintained
consistent demand and remained at capacity. We served over 1,500 patrons during this
period between our Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim lessons. We brought back
the Pre-Competitive Swim Class, which is our most advanced swim lesson program for
youth and our best feeder program into the competitive swim teams. We continued to
provide almost 250 hours of pool time to partner organization South Gate Aqua
Coalition (SGAC), Penguins Aquatic Club (PAC) and Lynwood Marlins Swim Team
(LMST). Additionally, as the home pool to the South Central Swim League’s fall league,
we hosted six meets during this season, with each meet bringing in about six local swim
teams, 400 local competitive swimmers, and over 600 spectators. We also served as
host to SGAC’s invitational USA swimming meet in September, which brought in
approximately 500 swimmers and their families and served as a fundraiser for the team.
Monthly in-service trainings emphasized emergency readiness, inclusive customer
service, and continuous improvement. We offered one Adult and Pediatric First
Aid/CPR/AED course and certified almost 15 community and staff members.
SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics, Masters Swim, and Aqua Blast fitness classes remained in
rotation, with Open Play Water Polo wrapping up in October. We had our second annual
Patti’s Pumpkin Plunge, our floating pumpkin patch, featuring arts and crafts, a pumpkin
decorating contest, games, prizes, music and more. We completely sold out at 200
participants.

The Aquatics Division sustained solid performance across all areas of operation during
the winter season, despite the seasonal challenges that typically affect participation and
facility maintenance. Our Learn-to-Swim program takes a break in the winter, but the
remaining programs saw steady attendance. Water fitness and therapeutic classes
continued to be a vital service, particularly for older adults. With almost 80 sessions
offered throughout the quarter, programs such as Aqua Blast, Aqua Aerobics, and
SeniorCise were well attended. The Pre-Competitive Swim Class remained strong, with
kids working hard to make the transition to the swim team. As one of the only indoor
pools open year-round, we were able to continue hosting local swim teams’ practices,
the South-Central Swim League’s winter swim league, and three USA Swimming meets
including the prestigious WAG Last Ditch Qualifier 2-day meet. This meet brought in
approximately 800 swimmers and over 1,500 spectators per day from more than a
dozen teams coming from the wider Los Angeles area. The Aquatics Team held the
second annual special holiday event, Surfing with Santa. This special day featured arts
and crafts, games, activities, prizes, and an opportunity to surf with Santa, Mrs. Claus,
and their elves. Event sold out with over 200 participants. We brought back our Senior
Lifeguard Training/Mentorship Program, with the goal of facilitating staff’s professional
development, skill enhancement, and career advancement. We had 8 mentees/mentors
participate in the 6-week program, which culminated with interviews for the Senior
Lifeguard position. During this quarter, the Aquatics Staff took the slower season as an
opportunity to deep clean the patron locker-rooms, staff areas, deck, and patio.

  Page 2 of 6
  8
 Things started to get busy again in the spring, especially with the return of our most
popular program, Learn-to-Swim Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim lessons for all
ages. March started off strong, with over 500 registrations. We also launched a new
program, Youth & Adult Swim Clinic with the focus of teaching participants water
competency and survival skills versus the traditional swim lesson curriculum. We had
over 20 participants and garnered a lot of interest for another round of the program.
During this period, we held three different Adult and Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED
courses and two different Lifeguard Certification courses. During May-June we
conducted our annual recertification course certifying 50 Lifeguards in American Red
Cross Lifeguarding with CPR/AED For Professional Rescuers, First Aid, Administering
Emergency Oxygen, and Bloodborne Pathogens Training.

This season, we again served as host to SCSL’s spring swim league with 6 meets on
our schedule. High school swim was also back, with South East High School practicing
at our pool. They had approximately 40 swimmers and four meets in their program. April
was especially eggciting, as we introduced another special aquatic event, Easter Splash
Fest. This event was met with much success, selling out at almost 250 participants. We
partnered with Raising Canes and SGAC and had an underwater egg hunt as well as
one in our grass area. We had goodie bags, arts and crafts, lawn games, and a giant
Easter bunny bounce house. Also in April, we partnered with a local school for their
College & Career Day. Aquatics Staff presented kids with goodie bags, info on how to
obtain a career within aquatics, and gave water safety & first aid demos. We were
honored to receive Council’s proclamation recognizing May as Water Safety Month. We
also celebrated International Water Safety Day on May 15 and hosted our 6 th Annual
Water Safety Bash on May 17. This yearly event is free and for the whole community.
In conclusion, the Aquatics Division made meaningful progress during the 2024–2025
year across all areas of service and is primed for more success throughout 2025-2026.

Sports Center/Fitness
The Sports Center Fitness membership program had a robust start to the new fiscal
year. Total memberships were over 4,400 participants with about 4,500 daily
admissions coming in during the 1st quarter. This momentum slowed from the 2nd into
the 3rd quarters with our membership database dropping down to 4,100 members
during the start of 2025. By the 4th quarter, we had a drastic drop to 2,500
memberships. The reduction in active memberships is attributed to the Department's
transition to a new credit card processing system, which now supports Tap to Pay
functionality.

The introduction of new Group Exercise classes has been well received. The Zumba
classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 11:15 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. continue to be very
popular. Our Seniorcise group exercise class increased its attendance by 100%; we had
to expand the class by creating an additional time slot on Fridays. Staff has worked hard
to develop age-appropriate exercises and programs that keep our Seniors engaged and
motivated. Step Aerobics and Advanced Yoga received additional time slots during the
week. We are also offering two new classes, Combo Boxing which is catered to our
older active population, and a High Intensity Interval Training class that is catered to
anyone that is looking for a fitness challenge. Currently, the Sports Center offers a

  Page 3 of 6
  9
 diverse range of over 35 weekly fitness classes that cater to all members and their
preferences.

Youth Fitness Programming continued to flourish, with Youth Olympic Weightlifting and
Game Changers reaching maximum capacity every session. These popular programs
attract many participants, thanks to their focus on enhancing muscular development and
coordination amongst youth. Our highly sought after Biggest Loser program, which
celebrated its 10-year anniversary, has once again reached full capacity. Over the
course of 12 long grueling weeks, participants challenge themselves every day through
a variety of staff led resistance training sessions and workouts. There are weekly weigh-
ins with opportunities to win prizes for weight loss and participation.

The Personal Training Program experienced stagnation, with a total of 752 hours of
training conducted over the fiscal year. The most popular package was the Private 12-
session, with 324 hours conducted this year. This can be attributed to clients entrusting
their Certified Personal Trainers to achieve their fitness goals and dedicating the time to
continue training with staff. The semi-private 16-session package recorded 288 hours of
training. To meet the demand that we typically see during the New Year months and the
summer months, we have expanded our team with more certified trainers. The program
remains highly requested and continues to receive excellent feedback from clients.

In January, we held our Annual Sports Center Open House, which was open to the
public and showcased all the facilities and fitness programming available. The event
featured abbreviated versions of Group Exercise classes, Personal Training
Assessments, and enjoyable sports activities for the entire family. Attendees also had
the chance to win prizes through staff-led activities throughout the day.

Our Spring Fit 5K returned for its 8th year. Bimbo Bakeries once again served as the title
sponsor, providing 800 performance tech shirts to all registered participants. The party
started at 6:00 a.m. with a DJ playing the latest hits. The Children’s Play Area had more
inflatables, and activities to win prizes. The accompanying vendor fair, featuring various
sponsors offering products and goodies, was also a major highlight. The Spring Fit 5K
remains a cornerstone event for our department and is set to grow even larger in the
future.

The 4th Annual Fun Run took place on July 19. The one-mile park course was filled with
inflatable obstacles, water slides, foam, and mud zones. This year, we had a Web Maze
for participants to crawl through and an Ice Crawl obstacle that participants really
enjoyed in the summer heat. Tampico came on board as a major sponsor, providing
high-performance tech shirts for all participants. The event included a vibrant vendor fair
with Tampico, the Youth Commission, Edwards Theaters and Raising Canes. With such
strong support, the Fun Run is set to continue growing alongside our other major
events.

Youth Sports
The 2024–2025 fiscal year proved to be both active and successful for our Youth Sports
division. Summer 2024 launched with our core Fundamental classes—Basketball,

  Page 4 of 6
  10
 Baseball, Soccer, Volleyball, and Multi-Sport all reaching full capacity. Sports classes
were held once a week for 45 minutes over a span of nine consecutive weeks. Each
program concluded with live scrimmages, a community potluck, and certificate
presentations. In addition, our contracted Karate classes were offered throughout the
summer and remained extremely popular with near capacity attendance.

Fall 2024 maintained strong momentum following an action-packed summer. Our core
class offerings remained consistent, once again reaching full capacity. On September
14, Karate instructor Juan Larios hosted his Annual International Karate-Do Shito-Ryu
Federation Tournament in the Sports Center Gymnasium, drawing over 80 athletes from
various regions and more than 400 spectators throughout the day. We also proudly
continued our partnership with Special Olympics, serving as the host site for their Fall
2024 L.A. County Games. The event welcomed over 500 athletes competing in Softball,
Soccer, Volleyball, and Golf, with hundreds of supporters and spectators in attendance.
Winter 2025 saw a slight dip in registration, which is typical for the season due to colder
weather and changing conditions. Despite this, our core class offerings remained
consistent and reached near full capacity. A highlight of the season was our first Sports
Excursion on February 13, where families attended the USC vs. UCLA women’s
basketball game, enjoying an exciting evening of live sports. On March 12, Glow in the
Dark Pickleball made its highly anticipated return. Staff transformed the gym using glow-
in-the-dark tape, paint, and equipment to create a vibrant, illuminated pickleball
experience. The family-friendly event ran from 6:30 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. and welcomed
over 75 participants. We closed out the winter session by proudly hosting our annual
Azalea Karate Tournament on March 23. The annual one day event brings in over 80
athletes and over 400 spectators throughout the tournament.
Spring 2025 saw a strong return in participation, with all classes reaching full capacity.
In response to high demand, class sizes were expanded from 15 to 20 participants.
From April 14 to April 18, we hosted a sold-out Spring Sports Camp where participants
engaged in a different sport each day, including basketball, soccer, volleyball, flag
football, and baseball. At the conclusion of the camp, each participant received a Sports
Camp T-shirt and sack pack to take home. On May 31, the South Gate Sports Center
proudly served as the host site for the Annual Special Olympics Basketball Competition.
The event welcomed 50 Special Olympic athletes and over 200 spectators. To close out
the spring season, our sports staff hosted an outreach booth at the Summer Kick-Off
Event on June 11. The event served as a Parks and Recreation resource fair where
community members had the opportunity to connect with staff and inquire about the
programs and services we offer.

Adult Sports
Our Adult Softball leagues successfully completed three full seasons this year. The
Men’s league, which takes place on Thursday evenings, had a total of 49 teams, while
the Co-ed league, played on Friday evenings, saw 62 teams participate throughout the
year. Additionally, we launched our first-ever Women’s Softball league on Monday
evenings, with 7 teams registering for the Fall 2024 season. Champions in each league
were awarded the redesigned championship hoodies or new ¾ zip long sleeves.
Our Open Play Volleyball program remains a popular option on Tuesday evenings, with
over 3,000 drop-in participants during the past fiscal year. Due to its growing popularity,

  Page 5 of 6
  11
 we are attempting to create a Co-ed Volleyball league this Fall.

We are anticipating the return of the Men’s Basketball league this Fall as well.
Registration is currently open, and the season is set to begin in September 2025.
Games will be held on Friday nights or Sunday mornings
